questions.q: The theory of comparative advantage was given by:
questions.explanation: Ricardo (1817), Principles of Political Economy and Taxation.

questions.q: According to the Heckscher–Ohlin theorem, a capital-abundant country exports:
questions.explanation: Countries export goods that use their abundant factor intensively.

questions.q: The Leontief paradox (1953) found that the USA exported:
questions.explanation: Contrary to H–O, US exports were relatively labour-intensive.
At constant goods prices, a rise in one factor raises output of the good intensive in it and reduces the other.

questions.q: Income terms of trade is defined as:
questions.explanation: Dorrance's income TOT measures the capacity to import.

questions.q: Marshall–Lerner condition for devaluation to improve trade balance is:
questions.explanation: The sum of the (absolute) export and import demand elasticities must exceed one.

questions.q: The absorption approach to BoP was given by:
The 'impossible trinity' says a country cannot simultaneously have:
options: Floating rate, inflation targeting and fiscal policy
Low inflation, high growth and full employment
Fixed exchange rate, free capital flows and independent monetary policy
questions.explanation: Only two of the three can be chosen at a time.

questions.q: Trade diversion in a customs union means:
options: Imports shift from a lower-cost outsider to a higher-cost member
Imports shift from a higher-cost member to a lower-cost outsider
Domestic production replaced by member imports

questions.q: Product life cycle theory of trade was given by:

questions.explanation: Jagdish Bhagwati (1958): export-led growth can worsen welfare through falling terms of trade.

questions.q: The WTO came into existence on:
questions.explanation: The Marrakesh Agreement was signed on 15 April 1994; WTO started on 1 January 1995.

questions.q: Exchange rate overshooting model was given by:
questions.explanation: Rudiger Dornbusch (1976), with sticky goods prices.

questions.q: Effective rate of protection is high when:
options: Tariff on output is higher than on inputs (tariff escalation)
Tariff on inputs is higher than on output
questions.explanation: ERP = (t − a·tᵢ)/(1 − a); low input tariffs with high output tariffs raise effective protection.
Economies of scale and love of variety give two-way trade in similar goods.
